title: Liverpool City Region Combined Authority – AI Summit
summary: Sum Vivas supplied multilingual AI digital humans to assist visitors at Liverpool's AI Summit on 21 November 2024; no source reports how many people they helped.
account: On 19 November 2024 the Liverpool City Region Combined Authority announced that multilingual, interactive digital humans would assist visitors and host its AI Summit on 21 November 2024. The supplier, Sum Vivas, named the assistants Ava, Alison and James. The Local Government Association account of 25 March 2025 reports that over 300 people attended the summit on 21 November 2024. It reports that the firm that showed the digital humans was in talks with local authorities about digital tour guides. In September 2025 the Combined Authority and Sum Vivas trialed a multilingual assistant named Jimmy at the Labour Party conference. In October 2025 they placed Jimmy at the Mersey Ferries terminal at Pier Head until early 2026, with a planned move to a train station. On 16 October 2026 Sum Vivas stated that its assistant Alison served at the first summit in 2024 and that James served at the second in 2025. The company reports that Jimmy was to join the 2026 summit. The accounts provide no measurements of changes in access to event information, in language barriers or in the organizers' workload. The assistants' contribution to attendance and investment interest is unknown. No source reports how many people the assistants helped.
purpose: Help summit attendees access information through multilingual AI interaction and support event hosting.

provenance.basis: SHA-256 of the public record, its assessments, and its displayed answers and notes, excluding its own identifier and the derived coverage summary.

fields.account: On 19 November 2024 the Liverpool City Region Combined Authority announced that multilingual, interactive digital humans would assist visitors and host its AI Summit on 21 November 2024. The supplier, Sum Vivas, named the assistants Ava, Alison and James. The Local Government Association account of 25 March 2025 reports that over 300 people attended the summit on 21 November 2024. It reports that the firm that showed the digital humans was in talks with local authorities about digital tour guides. In September 2025 the Combined Authority and Sum Vivas trialed a multilingual assistant named Jimmy at the Labour Party conference. In October 2025 they placed Jimmy at the Mersey Ferries terminal at Pier Head until early 2026, with a planned move to a train station. On 16 October 2026 Sum Vivas stated that its assistant Alison served at the first summit in 2024 and that James served at the second in 2025. The company reports that Jimmy was to join the 2026 summit. The accounts provide no measurements of changes in access to event information, in language barriers or in the organizers' workload. The assistants' contribution to attendance and investment interest is unknown. No source reports how many people the assistants helped.

produced_by: The planned service uses multilingual, interactive AI digital humans to assist attendees and host proceedings.
must_hold: Likely requirements include accurate event information, usable interaction, and suitable language support. These have not been validated as sufficient for a beneficial outcome.

echoes.setting: Second Liverpool City Region AI Summit, where the Sum Vivas assistant James was ready for delegates' questions.
Liverpool City Region AI Summit 2026, where the Combined Authority's digital visitor guide Jimmy was to introduce speakers and guide visitors on the summit website.
